title: Northeast Weather Update: Delta extends flexibility options for customers as Nor’easter continues
body_markdown:
A powerful Nor’easter is bringing strong winds and heavy rain across parts of the Northeast this weekend, including at Boston Logan International Airport (BOS). As a result of these conditions, a significant number of cancellations are expected for BOS on Sunday, Sept. 27. Delta automatically rebooks customers to the next best itinerary, and customers can make further changes via the Delta app and Delta.com.


Customers with impacted travel plans will receive direct communications from Delta with information about their options. Delta has issued travel waivers that allow eligible customers to change their flights without a fee. Customers are encouraged to proactively adjust their travel plans and can review waiver details here:


- [Northeast Weather Flexibility](https://www.delta.com/us/en/advisories/weather-alerts/northeast-weather-flexibility)


- [BOS Weather Flexibility](https://www.delta.com/us/en/advisories/weather-alerts/bos-weather-flexibility)


Weather in the region has constrained fuel deliveries into BOS. Delta is taking steps to help minimize impacts to customers, including operating in-bound aircraft to Boston with additional fuel allocated for its next scheduled flight and transporting additional fuel via tanker trucks to supplement fuel reserves where feasible.


Delta remains in close contact with Massport and other aviation stakeholders at BOS and will continue to monitor conditions closely and provide updates as needed.
